title: Unit rates and the better buy
summary: Partners find the price per ounce of two cereal boxes and argue which is the better buy, then use a constant walking speed to predict distance (6.RP.A.3b).

standard.text: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.

discourse: State a claim about which option is the better buy and support it with two unit rates that use the same unit (dollars per ounce for both boxes).
Explain where a unit rate comes from: which quantity was divided by which, and what the one in the unit rate refers to.
Answer a partner's counterclaim (the big box costs more) by separating the total price from the price for one unit.
sentence: Rate phrases with a singular noun after per: dollars per ounce, miles per hour (not per ounces).
Division described in words: I divided the price by the number of ounces to find the cost of one ounce.
Comparative claims with rates: The 18-ounce box costs less per ounce than the 12-ounce box, so it is the better buy.
word: Per, each and the slash read aloud: $/oz is said dollars per ounce; mph is said miles per hour.
The multiple-meaning word unit: one of something (unit rate), a measurement (ounce, mile) and a chapter of study.
Everyday shopping language that carries math meaning: better buy, deal, costs more, costs less, cheaper.

contentObjective: Students will find unit rates from ratios, including unit price and constant speed, and use them to compare options and predict values (6.RP.A.2, 6.RP.A.3b).
languageObjective: Students will argue which option is the better buy using per and each, supporting the claim with two unit rates in the same unit.

L1-2: The ___ box is the better buy. (big / small)
One ounce costs ___. (Word bank: per, each, ounce, costs less)
L3-4: I divided ___ by ___ to find the cost of one ___.
The ___ box costs $___ per ounce, but the ___ box costs $___ per ounce.
The ___ box is the better buy because it costs less for each ___.
L5-6: Even though the ___ box has a higher total price, its unit price is lower, because ___.
To compare fairly, both rates have to be in ___ per ___, so I ___.
At a constant rate of ___ per ___, in ___ we would expect ___, since ___.

vocabulary.definition: a ratio that compares two quantities with different units, such as miles and hours
vocabulary.morphology: from Latin rata 'fixed amount'; English rate and Spanish tasa are not related

vocabulary.definition: a rate that tells the amount for 1 of the second quantity, such as $0.25 per ounce
vocabulary.morphology: unit, from Latin unus 'one'; unitaria is a cognate, tasa is not

vocabulary.definition: the price for one unit of measure, such as one ounce or one pound
vocabulary.morphology: price and precio both come from Latin pretium 'value'

vocabulary.definition: how far something travels in a unit of time
vocabulary.morphology: Old English spēd; in science, velocity (velocidad) adds direction

vocabulary.definition: to split a quantity into equal groups or find how many groups fit
vocabulary.morphology: from Latin dividere, 'to separate'; the prefix di- means 'apart'

vocabulary.definition: a price or offer for buying something; a better deal gives you more for the same money
vocabulary.morphology: also a verb (to deal cards); ask which meaning fits

vocabulary.definition: every one, taken one at a time
vocabulary.morphology: followed by a singular noun: each ounce, each hour

activity.title: Best Buy Showdown
steps: Write two cereal boxes on the board: Box A is 12 ounces for $3.00; Box B is 18 ounces for $3.96. Ask each pair for a quick gut claim: which is the better buy?
Partner A finds the unit price of Box A and Partner B finds Box B. Each says the division aloud with a frame (I divided ___ by ___ to find the cost of one ___).
Partners write a claim and two pieces of evidence on paper. One partner argues for the other box on purpose; the other answers the counterclaim using unit price, not total price.
Switch contexts: a student walks 6 miles in 2 hours at a constant speed. Partners find the unit rate and use it to predict the distance in 5 hours (6.RP.A.3b).
Two pairs read their claim aloud; the class listens for per plus a singular unit and for both rates being in the same unit.

problems.prompt: Box A holds 12 ounces of cereal and costs $3.00. What is its unit price?
Box B holds 18 ounces of cereal and costs $3.96. What is its unit price?
Which box is the better buy? Support your claim with the unit prices.
problems.answer: Box B, the larger box, because it costs less per ounce than Box A.

problems.prompt: A student walks 6 miles in 2 hours at a constant speed. At that rate, how far will the student walk in 5 hours?

warmup: Write $/oz, mph, $/lb and words/min on the board. Partners take turns reading each one aloud as a full rate (dollars per ounce, miles per hour), then invent one real example for each, such as a car going 30 miles per hour. Finish by asking: in each rate, what does per mean? Collect the answer for each or in one.
